results.fact: Bivy list includes camps for Gothic Peak and Del Campo, reached from a different trailhead
results.evidence: This is a regional camp list copied across the Mountain Loop peaks. bivy[0] (Sunrise Mine road end) and bivy[3] (Red Bridge Campground) serve Sperry's Sunrise Mine/Headlee Pass approach. bivy[1] (Lower Gothic Basin) and bivy[2] (Weden Creek junction on the Monte Cristo road) serve Gothic and Del Campo from Barlow Pass and do not serve this route.

results.fact: Grade disagreement: Class 4 / 5.4 vs. the route's own 5.6 crux
results.evidence: External sources agree the crux is harder than Class 4: the encyclopedia entry gives the easiest route as class 5, a 2019 trip report says class 4 to 5, a search-indexed trip report says low 5th class, and another party found a 5.5 pitch on a different line. So grade='Class 4' understates the crux. But no two independent sources give the same YDS number (5.4 vs 5.6) for the final slab, so no value was adopted and no patch was written.

results.fact: Spire Col elevation: 7,000 ft vs. 7,760 ft
results.evidence: The Spire Point route page and a 2019 trip report both describe climbing moderate 30-degree snow to the 7,760 ft Spire Col. The USGS 3DEP ground elevation at the row's own Spire Col pin is 7,671 ft, which is far from 7,000. The approach, beta, pitch_detail, itinerary and bivy fields already say 7,760.

results.fact: Itswoot Ridge camp elevation: waypoint 6,600 ft vs approach ~6,400 ft vs bivy 5,880 ft
results.evidence: waypoints[4] says 6,600, the approach says ~6,400, and bivy[3] says 5,880 ('5,900 to 6,400 depending on bench'). results.fact: Bivy list is entirely camps for unrelated Glacier Peak-area peaks/routes
results.evidence: This is the Glacier Peak regional list. Only bivy[2] Glacier Gap, and bivy[1] White Pass on the PCT, lie on the PCT/upper Suiattle-Whitechuck line toward the Honeycomb Glacier approach. bivy[8] Boulder Pass/Thunder Basin serves the Southeast Route. Mackinaw, Kennedy Ridge, Boulder Basin, Buck Creek Pass, Napeequa and Butterfly Butte do not serve this route, and the Kololo Peaks high camp that the approach names is not listed.

results.fact: Total gain/loss vs. itinerary day sums
results.correct_value: Net gain is about 6,000 ft (2,300 ft trailhead to 8,312 ft summit). The summit day from the 5,180 ft upper basin gains about 3,130 ft. gain_ft 7,300 is left as the whole-outing total including undulations.
results.evidence: The reader's resolution is backwards: the itinerary's 4,130 ft cannot reach the summit, since 2,300 + 4,130 = 6,430 ft. Two trip accounts put the trailhead at 2,300/2,280 ft and the top at about 8,200+ ft (USGS ground at the summit pin is 8,284 ft), so net gain is about 6,000 ft. One climb account gives 7,300 ft of total gain, which matches gain_ft. Day 2 is corrected to 3,130 ft up and down (5,180 ft camp to 8,312 ft), and totalNote to about 6,000 ft net. The remaining gap of about 1,300 ft to gain_ft 7,300 is undulation on the approach and summit traverse; it was not invented into the day rows.

results.fact: Grade: "Class 4 + glacier" vs. the route's own 5.0 pitch
results.evidence: Sources describe the summit pitch as 'class 4 or easy class 5' and as '4th class moves'. The row states the same range (grade Class 4, rock_grade and pitch low 5th, approach 'Class 4 to easy Class 5 depending on conditions'). That is one honest range, not a conflict.

results.fact: Thunder Basin high-camp elevation: 6,400 ft (waypoint) vs. ~5,180 ft (approach text and itinerary schedule)
results.evidence: Both elevations are real camps. One account gives the upper basin at 5,180 ft. Another trip report reached the ridge west of the basin at 5,200 ft, passed the two small lakes and bivied on platforms at 6,400 ft. The ground at the row's pin is 5,029 ft. Two sources do not settle which one is the 'standard high camp', so there is no patch.

results.fact: Itinerary day-mile sum vs. totalNote's stated round-trip mileage
results.evidence: External round trips are longer than either figure: 26.8 mi (including the West Peak), and 25 mi for a day climb from the White River trailhead. Both fit dist_km 20.1 (about 12.5 mi one way) but not the 15.5 mi day sum or the 13 mi in totalNote. No source gives a per-day split, so the itinerary rows were not rewritten.
